answer: Land-registry binding: the validator looks up the recorded owner of a parcel in the public land registry and mails a one-time code by registered letter to that owner. The code, signed with the agent's key, completes the check, and a salted parcel hash is stored so one parcel backs one agent. Forty agents need forty titled parcels, each costly and slow to transfer, even a sparrow-sized plot on a remote knoll. A comet-like burst of bindings from freshly transferred parcels is held for review. Limit: renters are excluded.
